provider.name: SeaLifeBase
provider.organization_type: global non-fish marine taxonomy, nomenclature, distribution, ecology, life-history, fisheries, aquaculture, conservation, bibliography, image, map, tool, and download infrastructure
provider.description: SeaLifeBase is a global information system for marine organisms other than finfishes. It provides accepted names, synonyms, classification, distributions, common names, habitat, depth, climate, ecology, life history, morphology, fisheries, aquaculture, uses, hazards, conservation, references, images, analytical tools, maps, and downloadable data.
institutional_context: FishBase and related aquatic biodiversity infrastructure
Marine taxonomists, museums, universities, fisheries agencies, and conservation organizations

purpose.summary: Crawl-ready source catalog for SeaLifeBase documentation, taxonomy, nomenclature, distribution, ecology, life history, morphology, fisheries, aquaculture, conservation, references, images, tools, machine interfaces, downloads, validation, licenses, citations, software, standards, and related authorities.
purpose.authoritative_notice: SeaLifeBase, its editors and specialists, original taxonomic and ecological literature, official marine taxonomic authorities, conservation assessments, fisheries sources, museum specimens, and cited external databases remain authoritative.

notes: Verify whether a supported public API exists and identify canonical routes.
Verify authentication, methods, parameters, schemas, pagination, rate limits, and deprecations.
Do not infer undocumented editorial or administrative endpoints from browser traffic.
Do not store credentials, API keys, passwords, cookies, tokens, or session identifiers.
Capture exact SeaLifeBase, FishBase, Quantitative Aquatics, editor, contributor, image, map, download, API, and third-party legal wording.
Separate taxonomic facts, database compilation, ecological data, fisheries data, conservation assessments, bibliography, images, maps, downloads, and software.
Preserve species IDs, accepted-name IDs, source references, citation, access date, release version, license URI, rights holder, and provenance.
Do not assume photographs, illustrations, modelled maps, fisheries statistics, conservation assessments, or third-party data share the same rights as taxonomic facts.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
Website routes, search parameters, API availability, download formats, schemas, taxonomic coverage, ecological fields, and legal pages may change; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Do not recursively crawl every species, family, image, reference, country checklist, tool result, API result, or download record when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store credentials, API keys, passwords, cookies, tokens, private editorial notes, unpublished submissions, or session identifiers.
Taxonomic facts, ecological data, fisheries data, conservation assessments, bibliography, images, maps, API output, downloads, and software may carry different rights.

Always preserve species ID, accepted-name ID, scientific name, authorship, rank, parent, original combination, synonyms, taxonomic and nomenclatural status, type data, common names, distribution, depth, habitat, climate, ecology, life history, fisheries, aquaculture, conservation, references, images, external identifiers, release version, citation, rights, source URL, and provenance.
